blocks.heading: Close evaluator notebook
blocks.body: Use researched signals for Close — not interchangeable “great CRM” prose.

scenarios.title: Strengths that actually show up in research
scenarios.body: Inside sales and outbound teams that live on phone/email/SMS; Teams that want AI (Chloe) working leads inside the CRM; SMBs replacing disconnected dialer + CRM stacks

scenarios.title: Limitations that change the deal
scenarios.body: Growth (list price annual) and Scale (list price annual) per-user pricing is high versus pipeline-only CRMs; calling usage and premium phone lines add cost.; Advanced Chloe automation/workflows and predictive dialing depth are concentrated on Growth and Scale.; Calling is usage-based; AI credits are pooled monthly with plan caps and no rollover.

scenarios.title: Price / value hinge
scenarios.body: Value usually hinges on needing Solo or Essentials unlocks for contact management — not on brand familiarity.

sections.heading: Close ROI gate for evaluators
sections.body:
Evaluator thesis: Worth the seat spend if contact management + lead management are weekly must-haves. Counter-signal: Not worth it if Growth (list price annual) and Scale (list price annual) per-user pricing is high versus pipeline-only CRMs; calling usage and premium phone lines add cost. collide with your constraints.

Capability hinge for this product: contact management; lead management; pipeline management; deal management.

Integrations in research: WhatsApp Business, Slack.

Paid tiers that usually matter in evaluation: Solo, Essentials, Growth.

sections.heading: Who Close is worth it for — and who should avoid it
sections.body:
Worth it for: Inside sales and outbound teams that live on phone/email/SMS.

Avoid if: Buyers seeking the cheapest visual pipeline CRM.

If avoid signals dominate, start the alternative path with Pipedrive on the same job-to-be-done.

sections.heading: Close price/value and next evaluation step
sections.body:
Prove one real workflow on the documented free/trial path before arguing for Solo.

Tradeoff to accept consciously: Capability depth vs total cost of ownership on higher plans.

Next step: run contact management end-to-end, then decide.
